card.name: Comma before "including" after a risk term
card.fires_on: The comma right after a warning-section heading term or adverse-reaction phrase (e.g. "Hypersensitivity reactions," "can cause hepatotoxicity,"), where "including" or "which" is expected next. Also "most" in "most notably".

modes.label: Comma after adverse-event noun
modes.description: A comma following a named adverse reaction or toxicity, leading into a list introduced by "including".
modes.example: 5.4 Secondary Malignancies Secondary malignancies<<,>> including acute leukemia and myelodys

modes.label: "most" before "notably"
modes.description: The word "most" in general prose where "notably" or "often" style qualifiers follow.
modes.example: helped to popularize the subject through his books and lectures,<< most>> notably in The Feynman Lectures

card.writes: It favors words like "including", "many" and "often" that introduce examples, and disfavors "mainly" and "mostly".
card.plain: It marks the spot after a side-effect name where the text is about to say "including" and list examples.
